title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: RAG Failure Modes & Debugging
summary: RAG failures fall into five distinct categories, each with different root causes and fixes. Understanding the failure taxonomy is essential for systematic debugging — without a framework, engineers waste hours tuning the wrong component.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: RAG failures fall into five distinct categories, each with different root causes and fixes. Understanding the failure taxonomy is essential for systematic debugging — without a framework, engineers waste hours tuning the wrong component. The five failure categories are: **(1) Retrieval failures** — right content exists but isn't retrieved; **(2) Faithfulness failures** — retrieved context is correct but LLM hallucinates anyway; **(3) Relevancy failures** — answer is correct but doesn't address the actual question; **(4) Coverage failures** — corpus lacks the required information entirely; **(5) Infrastructure failures** — latency, errors, timeouts that affect reliability.

diagrams.title: Debugging a bad answer: walk the pipeline backwards
diagrams.explain: Debug **backwards** from the answer. If the right chunk was never retrieved, the problem is ingestion or retrieval; if it was retrieved but dropped, it is reranking or truncation; if the model saw it and still answered wrong, it is the prompt or model. Traces make each question a lookup instead of a guess.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
RAG FAILURE MODE TAXONOMY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

FAILURE CATEGORY 1: INGESTION FAILURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptom: "I don't have that information" for content that exists
Debug:   Self-retrieval test → score < 0.90 for known content
Causes:  
  ✗ Loader failed to parse PDF (encoding issue, scanned image)
  ✗ Text pre-processor stripped relevant content
  ✗ Chunk size created split in critical info location
  ✗ Embedding API failed silently (null vectors stored)
Fix:     Verify ingestion pipeline with spot-check logging

FAILURE CATEGORY 2: RETRIEVAL FAILURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptom: Content is indexed (self-retrieval passes) but not returned
Debug:   Query retrieval test → expected doc not in top-10
Causes:
  ✗ Query vocabulary ≠ document vocabulary ("cancel" vs "terminate")
  ✗ Query too short/vague → sparse embedding → poor ANN match
  ✗ Wrong embedding model for domain (general model for legal text)
  ✗ K too small (K=3, answer in position 4)
Fix:     Multi-query, HyDE, larger K, domain-specific embeddings

FAILURE CATEGORY 3: RANKING FAILURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptom: Correct doc in top-10 but not top-3 (used by LLM)
Debug:   Check rank of correct doc across query variations
Causes:
  ✗ ANN approximation errors
  ✗ Bi-encoder imprecision (needs cross-encoder)
  ✗ Score threshold excluding correct doc
Fix:     Add cross-encoder reranker, reduce threshold

FAILURE CATEGORY 4: GENERATION FAILURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptom: Correct doc retrieved but LLM still gives wrong answer
Debug:   Oracle test — manually insert correct answer in context
Causes:
  ✗ LLM hallucinating despite context (prompt too permissive)
  ✗ "Lost in middle" — correct doc at position 3-5
  ✗ Answer requires reading multiple chunks (need more context)
  ✗ Context truncated mid-sentence at chunk boundary
Fix:     Strict grounding prompt, reranking to position 1, overlapping chunks

FAILURE CATEGORY 5: CORPUS FAILURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptom: Query about topic not covered in any document
Debug:   All retrieval scores < 0.65
Causes:
  ✗ Document not added to corpus (missing ingestion)
  ✗ Topic genuinely not covered
  ✗ Information is too recent (stale corpus)
Fix:     Add missing docs, implement web search fallback,
         add periodic corpus refresh

DEBUGGING DECISION TREE:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Wrong answer received
        │
        ▼
[1] Self-retrieval: does expected content exist?
  NO  → INGESTION FAILURE → fix loader/chunking
  YES ↓
[2] Query retrieval: is expected doc in top-10?
  NO  → RETRIEVAL FAILURE → multi-query/HyDE
  YES (rank 6-10) → RANKING FAILURE → add reranker
  YES (rank 1-5) ↓
[3] Oracle test: insert answer directly in context, still wrong?
  YES → GENERATION FAILURE → fix prompt grounding
  NO  → content present but LLM logic error → fix prompt structure
```

quiz.question: How do you detect and fix the "wrong chunk" problem — retrieval returns adjacent but not exact content?
options: LLMs attend primarily to beginning and end of context; middle documents get less attention.
Test retrieval recall per language separately.
Three root causes: (1) Vocabulary mismatch — domain jargon not well-represented in general embedding model (BAAI/bge-large may not know medical abbreviations); (2)…
Adjacent chunk problem: the answer is in chunk N+1 or N-1, but the query retrieves chunk N.
quiz.explanation: Adjacent chunk problem: the answer is in chunk N+1 or N-1, but the query retrieves chunk N. Fixes: (1) Parent-child chunking — store small child chunks for retrieval, return parent chunks for generation; (2) Sliding window chunking with 20-25% overlap; (3) Sentence-window retrieval — retrieve by sentence, expand to surrounding window. --- Q3–Q10 Summary:

quiz.question: What is "lost in the middle" and how do you detect it?
options: Test retrieval recall per language separately.
Adjacent chunk problem: the answer is in chunk N+1 or N-1, but the query retrieves chunk N.
When retrieved docs contain the answer but LLM generates wrong content: (1) check if prompt explicitly forbids external knowledge; (2) test with temperature=0…
LLMs attend primarily to beginning and end of context; middle documents get less attention.
quiz.explanation: LLMs attend primarily to beginning and end of context; middle documents get less attention. Detect: test the same query with target doc at position 1, 3, 5 — if accuracy drops at position 3, you have lost-in-the-middle. Fix: always put highest-scored docs at positions 1 and last; use contextual compression to reduce total context; use reranking to ensure best doc is at position 1.

quiz.question: How do you debug "hallucination despite good retrieval"?
options: Adding as much context as possible (K=20, large chunks) thinking more context = better answers.
Adjacent chunk problem: the answer is in chunk N+1 or N-1, but the query retrieves chunk N.
Self-retrieval test: embed chunk content, search for it — it must return at rank 1.
When retrieved docs contain the answer but LLM generates wrong content: (1) check if prompt explicitly forbids external knowledge; (2) test with temperature=0…
quiz.explanation: When retrieved docs contain the answer but LLM generates wrong content: (1) check if prompt explicitly forbids external knowledge; (2) test with temperature=0 (stochastic hallucination); (3) check for "lost in middle" (top doc at bad position); (4) verify retrieved doc isn't cut off (truncated mid-sentence); (5) test with a smaller, more focused context (compression).

quiz.explanation: Three root causes: (1) Vocabulary mismatch — domain jargon not well-represented in general embedding model (BAAI/bge-large may not know medical abbreviations); (2) Distributional shift — embedding model trained on web text, corpus is formal technical documents; (3) Cross-lingual gaps — multilingual queries underperform on English-only embedding models.
